object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: An individual in the system, identified by a person ID. Persons form the base category that includes employees and other individuals.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: PersonId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to each person in the system.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person who works for the organization. Every employee is also a person, sharing the same identification scheme.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with additional management responsibilities, identified through the same person ID as their employee and person status.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit that contains employees. Each department has a unique department code and name.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.

object_types.name: DepartmentCode
object_types.definition: The unique code that identifies a department.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a department, such as Payroll or Field Operations. No two departments share the same name.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.
We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.
Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.
A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.
Each department has a department code.
Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

ambiguities.description: Identification of Manager: Does every manager have a unique identifier, or do managers inherit the person ID from their employee status? The transcript states managers are identified the same way as employees (through person ID), but it is unclear whether a manager can be identified independently or whether the manager role depends entirely on the person ID.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of Department-Manager relationship: The transcript states 'A manager manages at most one department' but does not explicitly address the reverse: can a department be managed by multiple managers (e.g., co-managers) or must each department have exactly one manager or possibly no manager at all?

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of Employee-Department relationship from the department side: The transcript states 'Departments have many employees' but does not explicitly state whether every department must have at least one employee or whether a department can exist with zero employees.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.

ambiguities.description: Temporal scope of employee-department assignment: The relationship 'Every employee works in exactly one department' describes current state. It is unclear whether the model should track historical assignments, effective dates, or whether reassignments are to be captured.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department.

ambiguities.description: Relationship between Manager status and Department management: The model captures that managers can manage departments, but it is unclear whether a manager MUST also work in the department they manage, or whether a manager could work in a different department while managing another.

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department.
